leaves.search_question: Is there a uniquely grounded entity or scene whose presence or explicit absence is directly decidable in one time scope?
leaves.construction_rule: Use only an explicit presence-versus-absence assertion about the same grounded entity and time scope.
hard_exclusions: Do not treat a wrong category as non-existence.
Do not construct from mere omission or a non-exhaustive description.

leaves.search_question: Is there a uniquely grounded entity whose object category is directly visible and admits a plausible wrong category?
leaves.construction_rule: Keep the same entity anchor and change only its normalized category.
hard_exclusions: Color, clothing, age appearance, and gender appearance are attributes.
Do not replace the entity anchor.

leaves.search_question: Is there a fixed time scope containing a directly countable set of distinct visible entity tracks?
leaves.construction_rule: Keep the same entity set and time scope and change only the integer count.
hard_exclusions: Do not use event repetition counts.
Do not use ambiguous, occluded, or changing sets.

leaves.search_question: Is there a uniquely grounded entity or scene with a directly observable unary property?
leaves.construction_rule: Keep the same entity and attribute key and replace only the observable value.
hard_exclusions: Do not use intentions, personality, atmosphere, or other subjective properties.
Dynamic events belong to ActionPredicate.

leaves.search_question: Are two grounded entities in a directly decidable static spatial relation within one snapshot-like time scope?
leaves.construction_rule: Keep subject and object anchors fixed and change only the static relation predicate.
hard_exclusions: Do not use relations that require cross-frame motion to establish.
Do not swap subject and object anchors.

leaves.search_question: Is there a uniquely grounded dynamic event whose action predicate is directly decidable?
leaves.construction_rule: Keep the event, subject, object, and interval fixed and replace only the action predicate.
hard_exclusions: Do not construct role-binding errors.
Do not replace the event participants.

leaves.search_question: Are two supported component events both visible with a directly decidable relative temporal order?
leaves.construction_rule: Keep both event anchors fixed and reverse only their normalized order.
hard_exclusions: Do not infer causality.
Do not replace either component event.

leaves.search_question: Does the original video contain a real, temporally bounded camera or editing change whose operation is directly observable rather than inferred from object motion?
leaves.construction_rule: The supported source fact must assert one actual camera or editing change in the original video. Keep that exact camera-event anchor and interval fixed, then replace only the camera predicate with an incompatible camera/edit change or with no_camera_change to deny the observed change.
hard_exclusions: A stationary shot or generic framing description is not an eligible supported source fact because it does not identify an actual camera or editing change.
Do not infer camera motion from one actor or object changing image position or apparent size; require global frame, parallax, optical, focus, framing, viewpoint, or edit evidence.
Actor or object motion belongs to ActionPredicate.
A static arrangement between entities belongs to StaticRelation.
A visible unary property belongs to AttributeValue.
An entity appearing or disappearing through scene action belongs to EntityExistence; only a shot/edit transition belongs here.
Relative order between two grounded events belongs to TemporalRelation.
A semantic scene change is not by itself a camera change.
Do not change the camera-event anchor or interval.
